title: CI had not run for 46 days: two stacked breakages, the second hiding the first
detail: Verified by the controller over all 554 runs: 529 failure, 23 success, last success 2026-07-22T22:53:02Z. Green on run 34053229048 with all six corpus guards naming themselves (6 verified, 0 skipped) and 2647 tests passed.

title: A second video-port write in one instruction re-charges the first write's stall, 40 percent over-billed
detail: now_mclk is set once per instruction while fifo_slot_clock is absolute. Six stalling writes charge 967 cycles against a true 281. data_read_at does it correctly one function away. Every existing test stops at the fifth write.

title: The Z80 reset line is a hold, not a reset: a halted sound driver never restarts
detail: Measured with two controls. Z80 exposes no reset method; the core is constructed once and never re-initialised. The rule was written into docs/2026-07-22-sound-stack-recon.md:224 in July with 'pin it, do not let it drift' and never implemented.

title: About 560 real Z80 encodings panic uncontained; one byte in a guest driver kills the process
detail: Measured by executing every prefixed encoding under catch_unwind: ED 20, DD 46, FD 46, DDCB 224, FDCB 224. No catch_unwind anywhere in production. A commercial ROM reached this class before.

title: Every replay frame renders a full attributed scanline and discards it, to produce three status bits
detail: wants_scanlines defaults to false and oracle-replay's Fanout overrides neither. The tool whose pitch is one playthrough instead of many pays a discarded raster every frame.

title: Three guard tests and the guards they test both vanish under --release
detail: Controller re-measured: 11 tests in debug, 8 in release. They do not report as ignored; the count drops silently.

title: A reset could strand or roll back the owner's battery save
detail: Not hosted-only, so the booked mitigation did not cover it. The existing guard asserted on the machine and never the file, and its helper never ran the debounce. Fixed structurally in Bus::call_stamped; two new rows read the real .srm and each goes red naming the file.

title: The request side of the wire has a machine-readable contract and no differential against it
detail: 57 integer bounds in the fragments; jsonschema is a dev-dependency only; every bound re-implemented by hand in 62 handlers. 21 of 62 methods have no negative-value test. One Engine on one thread with no catch_unwind.

title: The listing-freshness guard is blind to two of the three populations it gates
detail: Compares address rows only; equates and phase are disjoint populations, and lookup_equate attaches this very caveat. Change an equate's value and the server answers the old number quietly. Zero equate coverage in the freshness suite.

title: The most-repeated safety claim in the tree names a mechanism that does not exist
detail: Repeated in eight source comments, two escalating to 'none may ever be added'. No compile-fail harness exists in the workspace and no test asserts the signature. A correct example naming a real mechanism sits 4000 lines away in the same crate.

title: The drift gate landed this morning covers none of the eleven symbols the panel landed this afternoon needs
detail: Controller re-measured: 25 rows, zero matching Parallax|Raster|BgAnim, against a working control. Controller correction: the FIXTURES are the stale side, not the panel.

title: A per-line scroll value is fetched once per pixel, 320 times more often than it can change
detail: plane_hscroll takes no x and does two VRAM reads. The line-hoisted copy already sits in ASlotCtx three lines away. Confirmed in the shipped binary by objdump.

title: A damaged-but-binding symbol file is disclosed on three surfaces and silent on the two that answer programs
detail: Load a truncated listing in the window and you get a warning; load the same file over the socket and it is accepted silently. Names then resolve to a plausible, healthy-looking, wrong routine.

title: The completed-frame reader exists four times and only the copy scheduled for deletion is tested
detail: The retirement deletes the only tested copy and leaves two untested, one of which backs emulator/screenshot and every hosted client.

title: A doc says callers must not reach this arm and the sole caller does
detail: Space::Z80 is a live selector entry. The covering test picks Space::Vram and asserts a message the Z80 path fails.

title: The I/O decode rule is applied on the read path and contradicted on the write path
detail: Read cites its evidence; write states the opposite rule citing nothing. Word writes are unaffected, which is why no golden catches it. The seat reported the contradiction and refused to adjudicate the hardware question.

title: A bounded list bypasses the blessed helper its sibling uses on the identical bound
detail: No total, no returned, no limit, where the helper's own doc makes all three the rule and the schema makes them required. The fragment was transcribed to the hand-rolled shape, so conformance is structurally blind.

title: Nothing in the sweep was exercised against a running emulator, window, or full suite
detail: Charter rules 2 to 4, with the owner's window live throughout. Every runtime-dependent claim is tagged rather than asserted.

title: The 20-agent cap degraded three seats that ran, not only the five it delayed
detail: A2, ERR and P2 each had helper agents refused and pattern-swept engine.rs and ui.rs rather than reading them. All three disclosed it unprompted. Coverage is narrower than 22 seats implies.

title: F-THREE-MASKED-RENDERERS is not a live drift risk: both divergences are unreachable
detail: The three copies differ in two guards, but both depend on a short or empty row and resolve_line_masked sets width unconditionally, including on the display-disabled early return. Dead code. What survives is the missing assertion.

title: The audio-repair door-that-runs-no-repair lead is refuted
detail: Every machine-replacing door runs it, structurally, in both windows. The bus-notification half of the same lead was confirmed and is a separate finding.

title: land.sh G1 is not the only thing between a fresh worktree and a false green
detail: G1 only counts files; the real backstop is six in-suite refusals armed by CI=1 that check named manifests. Residual: a human typing the raw cargo command gets CI unset and every corpus row skips invisibly.

title: PIN.tsv is not restated anywhere in code
detail: No sha, byte count or freeze revision from the pin is hardcoded in Rust or tools. The pin is read, never restated.

title: 576 test functions added over 250 commits, 11 removed, zero silent deletions
detail: Six were renamed because the behaviour changed. No guard was deleted and left claimed as live in code.

title: Layer and LayerMask cannot gain a variant without declaring it everywhere
detail: ALL is test-guarded, every match exhaustive with no catch-all, and targets() derives the wire names with a test pinning the derivation against the vendored fragment in both directions.

title: DIMENSIONS.tsv is derived and re-verified every run, not transcribed
detail: Re-measured through SymbolTable against independently pinned bytes, with a positive control that panics on an uncovered probe kind.

title: Symbol resolution is a binary search over a pre-sorted index and the Arc clones are refcount bumps
detail: Expected to find a linear scan and did not.

title: The SAT cache's two-copies-of-one-truth is correct by design
detail: The staleness being modelled is the hardware's own, so recomputation would be the wrong answer. Documented with its reason and guarded by a test.

title: Around twenty idiom candidates checked and cleared as deliberate, each with its reason in place
detail: Includes a hand-formatted address whose sum can exceed u32 and five of six debug asserts carrying a stated reason, one naming the test that would actually catch it.

title: The Z80 reset line is a hold, not a reset: a halted sound driver never restarts

Eleven mutations, each red on the row under test, including the silent-forever case. End-to-end test drives the real bus and observes EXECUTION, not a register or a latch. singlestep_z80 708,000 cases, 0 failures. The deferral that licensed this stated its own expiry condition in July and nobody returned; that doc now carries the pin.

title: The drift gate landed this morning covers none of the eleven symbols the panel landed this afternoon needs
detail: Fixed. Manifest 25 rows to 85; the control that read 0 now reads 65. Twelve dimensions pinned across four listings, including three pinned as ABSENT so a symbol becoming present also reddens. Gate deliberately left GREEN: the agent argued, correctly, that writing the engine's current addresses into a column the manifest binds to the frozen bytes would convert a recovery gate into a permanently-red currency gate and force the open owner decision rather than leave it open.

title: About 560 real Z80 encodings panic uncontained; one byte in a guest driver kills the emulator
detail: Closed by SERVING all 560, not by containing them. Stage 1 made refusal structural (a fault latch checked ahead of interrupt acceptance and the HALT idle; deliberately NOT halted=true, which is architectural state an interrupt would wake, vectoring into the program the core just refused). Stage 2 implemented every class graded against the vendored SingleStepTests corpus at pin ebe1875d: ED mirrors 20/20, IXH/IXL 92/92, DDCB/FDCB register-copy 448/448, 1000 cases per encoding, green on the first run; whole z80 suite 1268 files / 1,268,000 cases. New gate crates/oracle-core/tests/z80_guest_bytes_never_panic.rs steps all 1524 complete encodings plus 4096 two-prefix chains under catch_unwind: 0 panicked, 1524 executed, 0 refused. The deferral's stated reason was itself the defect: the in-tree comment said a documented-mode corpus never fetches them, true of our FILES list and false of the corpus, where all 560 answer keys existed at the pinned SHA (560 HEAD probes, 404 detector control). Controller verified with a mutation in a class the agent did not touch: forcing LD IXL,n to write IXH reddens the corpus run naming IX [DD 2E 0000] while unprefixed 2e.json still passes 1000/1000. Manifest checked as a set: 560 added, 0 of 708 removed; 1268/1268 sha256 OK. Landed GREEN 80/80 legs. Residual: Z80::refuse now has zero callers because exhaustive matches serve everything, kept deliberately with the reason at the definition. TAGGED, needs foreground: a real driver using IXH/IXL playing audibly; and a CR for a typed z80Fault key, since today it is a conditional caveat and the contract forbids parsing caveats.

title: Three guard tests and the guards they test both vanish under --release
detail: debug_assert! guards promoted to assert! in the fixture builder, plus three sibling guards of the same class in the same file. Controller measured both profiles independently, before and after: testrom:: scope was 11 tests in debug and 8 in release (dropping silently, not reporting as ignored), and is 11/11 after. oracle-core 1129 passed 0 failed in BOTH profiles. No pin was added and none is possible: once the guard is a plain assert! the profile split does not exist, and the three de-gated #[should_panic] rows ARE the regression guard, so fix and guard are one edit. Proven by demoting a guard back to debug_assert!, which reddens two rows under --release rather than deleting them (9 passed 2 failed = 11). Swept: no #[cfg(debug_assertions)] remains on any test row in crates/.

title: schema_conformance.rs's loud refusal is silent: libtest eats the SKIPPED banner
detail: ADDED TO THE LEDGER AS FIXED: this packet HIGH had no ledger row while it was open, so it never appeared in an open tally. Recorded now so the fixed record is true; it does not change any open count. The house fd-2 helper from c301f89 applied to the file that c301f89's own follower (mcp_tool_sweep.rs) names as its exemplar, which the original sweep had missed. Controller verified both directions firsthand: on main a plain cargo test prints nothing at all; at the fix the same command prints the 13-line SKIPPED banner. Worse than elsewhere because no runner sets $AETHER_CONTRACT_SCHEMA or $AETHER_CONTRACT_REPO, so the skip branch is the one every landing takes. Residual, NOT closed by this: nothing has still ever confirmed the pinned contract revision exists upstream. H5 made the refusal audible; it did not make the confirmation happen.

title: The request side of the wire has a machine-readable contract and no differential against it
detail: Fixed by tests/request_bounds.rs, a differential that PARSES every numeric bound out of the vendored bus-protocol.schema.json at test time and sends one step outside each end; no bound is written down anywhere in the test. Six gates: the differential, a two-ended in-bounds anti-vacuity control, a coverage ledger requiring baselines-union-uncovered to equal the derived bounded set in both directions, an enumerable-surface report, an anti-rot check on the one registered divergence, and a hard-wired witness that the walk reads the document. MEASURED: 58 declared bound sites over the 32 advertised methods that carry any request bound; 41 sites covered, 17 declared UNCOVERED (the six object methods, which need a loaded act); 70 probes, all refused -32602 BY NAME, 0 accepted, 0 unmeasured. Full crate suite 609 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored. THE FINDING'S NUMBERS WERE ALL WRONG in the direction that mattered: not 57 bounds but 60 sites (58 on advertised methods), and not 62 handlers re-implementing bounds but 32 -- the other 30 advertised methods declare no request bound at all, so the surface was half the size reported. More importantly the premise was wrong: no handler anywhere the differential can reach defaults an out-of-bounds value instead of refusing it. emulator/step was the exception, not the sample. TWO NEW FINDINGS from running it. (1) F-Z80READ-LEN0-UNSERVEABLE: z80_read's fragment declares len minimum 0 -- alone among every len on the surface -- so len:0 is a request the contract PERMITS; the server answers bytes "0x"; result.bytes is $defs/hex whose pattern ^0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+$ requires at least one digit. No conformant reply exists, the server may not refuse it and cannot answer it. Nothing in the tree had ever sent it. BLOCKED as a fix (both remedies are the contract owner's and this parcel is hermetic); registered in KNOWN_UNSERVEABLE with anti-rot, and a mutation proved that widening the hex pattern to ^0x[0-9A-Fa-f]*$ is sufficient. (2) A false green inside the differential itself, caught only by its own in-bounds control: a write_memory baseline that paired disp with addr was refused -32602 naming disp -- for the param's COMPANY, not its VALUE -- so the out-of-bounds probe read as enforcement without ever reaching the bound. The by-name rule is necessary and not sufficient. Every gate proven red-first with the mutation quoted from disk and restored from a committed baseline: removing step's count floor reproduces the founding defect (ACCEPTED x2); stripping the field name out of hex::parse_count turns 14+ probes UNNAMED; tightening sprites.limit to 2 reddens the control alone while the differential stays green; adding a bound to an unruled fragment reddens three gates; widening $defs/hex reddens the anti-rot. Left open and enumerable: the six object methods (F-OBJ-BOUNDS-UNPROBED, 17 sites), and two ceilings the max control does not send -- press.frames 1000 (F-PRESS-CEILING-UNEXERCISED, the harness's one-frame budget legitimately refuses it) and wait_for_break.timeoutMs 300000 (F-WAITBREAK-CEILING-UNEXERCISED, reasoned not measured, since measuring costs five minutes). The finding's catch_unwind clause is true and deliberate: catch_unwind appears in no shipping crate, which oracle-core/src/z80/mod.rs argues for explicitly -- containment is structural refusal, not a wrapper at the handler boundary. Not treated as a defect here.

title: A per-line scroll value is fetched once per pixel, 320 times more often than it can change
detail: Fixed. plane_sample and plane_pixel now take the line's h-scroll as a parameter; the per-line hoist lives in LineCtx (was ASlotCtx), built once in resolve_line_masked and pixel_attribution_masked. The finding's own prescription was half a fix: it said the hoisted copy 'already sits in ASlotCtx three lines away', which is true for plane A only -- plane B is sampled on the same dots and had no hoisted copy at all, so reusing the existing field would have left half the per-dot fetches in place. The struct was renamed because a struct called ASlotCtx carrying b_hscroll would be a lie. Measured in the shipped binary by objdump: Vdp::plane_sample 201 -> 140 instructions. Picture parity is the whole acceptance test and it holds byte-for-byte -- all 6 golden_frames pins unchanged (incl. scene 4 hscroll_modes, this finding's own subject), plus a 600-frame real-ROM differential over fixtures/aeon/s4.debug.bin, 129,024,000 raw RGB bytes cmp-identical.

title: One hardware integer division per plane per dot, from a Vec::len() used as a modulus
detail: Fixed. Vdp::vsram_word wrapped with (idx * 2) % self.vsram().len(); len() on a Vec is a runtime value, so that was a real div, reached once per plane per dot through plane_vscroll. It now wraps by the constant VSRAM_SIZE -- the same authority Vdp::data_read already uses for its own VSRAM reads and the only length Vdp::new ever allocates -- with a debug_assert_eq! stating that assumption at the point it is made. Located by search, not by the filing, which recorded no line. Confirmed in the shipped binary by objdump: Vdp::plane_vscroll carried 4 div instructions before and 0 after, and the whole binary went 80 -> 76. In the render path the modulus never actually fired (H40's widest VSRAM index is 39, byte 78 of 80) -- nothing had told the compiler that. Same parity evidence as H12: 6 golden pins unchanged and a 129 MB byte-identical real-ROM framebuffer differential.

title: WORK_RAM_LO is two different numbers under one name, and only one copy carries the derivation
detail: NOT a documentation fix, and the packet was right to flag that. Decided from source, not from either comment: oracle-core's bus decodes work RAM as 0xE0_0000..=0xFF_FFFF and folds the index with addr & (RAM_SIZE-1) at bus.rs:1048 (read) and :1170 (write) -- one 64 KiB chip, 128 mirrors -- so $E00000 is the DECODE and $FF0000 is merely the mirror the listing's FFFFxxxx symbols spell. oracle-aether's copy was right; oracle-replay's was wrong and widened to match. Live defect closed: stack_in_work_ram returned None for an A7 in any lower mirror, so decode_trap (runner.rs:760) booked a perfectly readable frame as StackNotInWorkRam. ram_u8/ram_u32 already folded correctly, so the range check was the only thing disagreeing with the hardware. The hazard runs BOTH ways -- unifying onto the narrow spelling would silently shrink the Aether server's RAM window -- which is why it is gated rather than tidied. GATED: the_work_ram_window_covers_every_mirror_the_bus_decodes, written before the fix and red on committed code (left: None, right: Some(0x00E00000)); it asserts the two spellings of one byte agree, so the narrowing unification goes red. oracle-replay 76 + 13 passed / 0 failed.

So F5 left the mode armed holding the OUTGOING listing's archetype NAMES, which object_spawn re-resolves at call time: the click succeeds at a different address (92.6% of shared s4.lst/s4.debug.lst symbols name a different one). A plain reset (Tab/F1) deliberately does NOT disarm -- it keeps the cartridge -- so the old doc was wrong on that half too. The doc now carries the exhaustive three-row table of listing-replacing sites and says the better shape (derive armed-ness from the listing generation) is not built and why. Gate: the_bounds_check_covers_every_offset_field_the_layout_declares reads the module's own source and fails for an offset field nobody thought to list. TWO CORRECTIONS to the finding as booked: (a) the damage is an index PANIC, not a byte written into the next ring -- Rust bounds-checks slice indexing in every profile; (b) a '-1'-spelled equate does NOT reach the overflow, since a 32-bit assembler spells it $FFFFFFFF and that does not overflow u64. The wrap needs a 16-hex-digit equate and the parser's own doc records 8 as the widest ever seen, so the incomplete-coverage half is the live one. The wrap was still demonstrated: with the old arithmetic restored, --release returned Ok for a u64::MAX offset (the confident pass) while dev panicked with 'attempt to add with overflow'.

Drained::symbols is a repair RECEIPT (symbols_changed || rom_changed), so it is true after emulator/reset, which KEEPS the listing; and own.symbols_changed is raised by this window's OWN preview, because screen_pick takes a checkpoint per arm and checkpoint_restore bumps symbols_generation unconditionally -- so keyed on the union, arming spawn mode raised the signal that retracted it on the next drain. Both caught by a control written before the gate (a_quiet_iteration_leaves_the_object_mode_armed). Published fact is now Drained::listing_replaced_by_a_client = report.symbols_changed alone. The sentence is one const (spawn::DISARMED_BY_LISTING_CHANGE) quoted by both windows. Ring mode deliberately survives a listing change: it reads its bounds at click time. title: Two mutually-exclusive click modes kept as two bools, and the clearing happens before the fallible arm

Both refusal arms driven with a different fixture each (-32012 no listing, -32013 a listing naming no ObjDef_), and each proved independently red under the restored ordering. DESIGN CALL on the brief's 'a type that cannot represent both-at-once': NOT taken, with reason. Object armed-ness lives inside oracle_frontend::spawn::Mode, a type shared with the frontend, so an enum here would not remove the second bool -- Mode::is_armed() would remain independently readable and the enum would be a THIRD source of truth for one fact, which is this parcel's own defect class. title: An address-error abort reports executed: true
detail: TWO bugs, not one, and the brief's one-line fix is insufficient. (1) install_address_error never set suppresses_trace, though three doc sites beside it say it does; StepOutcome::executed is defined as !suppresses_trace, so an aborted instruction reported executed: true -- a faulting JSR classifies as a Call, pushes a phantom frame, and step_over waits for a return that cannot come. The same flag is the trace-suppression predicate, so a vector-9 trace also pended after a fault (M68000UM 6.3.8 forbids it). (2) step_reporting read recipe.suppresses_trace() BEFORE run_to_completion. The decode-time entries (illegal/privilege/line-A/F) set the flag at decode and read correctly; an address-error abort cannot set it until the recipe RUNS, so setting the flag alone leaves both readings exactly as wrong as before. That ordering is also the mechanism behind the packet's note that the existing guard validated the search and not the question: the decode-time trace test passes with the read in either position. Fixed at both ends. title: The machine runs 0.129 % fast: "60 Hz" is the label, 59.9227 Hz is the value
detail: Fixed exactly, not merely better. samples_per_frame = sample_rate/60 was samples per 1/60 s while NAMED per frame; an NTSC frame is 896040 mclk = 1/59.92274 s = 735.9476 samples at 44.1 kHz. Because both windows make the audio device the master clock, emulated fps = sample_rate / samples-per-frame exactly, so 735 pinned the machine at 60.000 Hz -- 278 extra emulated frames per hour, growing linearly. Player-only; headless paces on nothing. The same error made FM and PSG pitch 0.129 % sharp (~2.2 cents), since both chips advance one output sample's worth of phase per next_sample. DERIVED, NEVER COPIED: MCLK_HZ = PSG_CLOCK * MCLK_PER_Z80_CYCLE = 53693175 Hz, exact because the PSG shares the Z80's mclk/15 leg and 3579545 is the NTSC colour subcarrier; the FM leg is the cross-check and deliberately not the source (YM2612_CLOCK is the rounded 7670453 the VGM header carries, x7 lands 4 Hz low). No 59.9227 and no 53693175 is typed. EXACT rather than rounded: a constant 736 would have cut the error 18x (278 -> 15 frames/hour) and been the same defect with a nicer number; samples_in_frame is the Bresenham difference of two exact running totals, so the count alternates 735/736 and never leaves the rational by more than one sample. The core was already built for it -- Ym2612Synth::begin_frame has always TAKEN the count as a parameter. The AudioSink field is gone entirely: holding one number was the defect. oracle-frontend::audio::frame_samples was 2*(sample_rate/60), a second disagreeing opinion about frame length, and now delegates to nominal_samples_per_frame (rounded, documented as a SIZING unit, never a rate). GATES: an_hour_of_frames_carries_an_hour_of_samples_at_the_true_ntsc_rate observes the RENDER path (counts off the rendered buffer, not the helper -- a render_frame that ignored samples_in_frame would pass a helper-only test), bounded at 600 frames because an hour of real FM+PSG rendering is ~115 s of suite time, with an anti-vacuity check that two different frame lengths were produced and a control that fails if the row and the 278-frames/hour finding drift apart; the_per_frame_count_straddles_the_exact_rational_and_never_drifts pins the mechanism a rounded constant would not have. Mutations proven red on disk: M-H8a (restore sample_rate/60) reds all three rows; M-H8b (the ROUNDED constant) reds the straddle row (736,736) vs (735,736) and the hour row's anti-vacuity, which is the pair showing exact is distinguished from merely-better. NO GOLDEN MOVED. Two frontend expectations did, both reported and neither regenerated (commit 408ff4c) -- and the second is a finding of its own: occupancy_feedback_eliminates_the_underruns_an_open_loop_producer_guarantees required the open-loop producer to underrun >=5 % of callbacks, a floor that was arithmetic on the DEFECTIVE frame length (0.6213 % deficit -> 5.2 %; the true 0.4932 % -> 4.0 %). That control sat within 4 % of its own vacuity and one correct change tipped it over. It was NOT re-tuned to the new edge; its load-bearing assertion is now threshold-free (produced < demanded over the run -- what a deficit IS, true at any size, false the instant the producer keeps up), with the percentage kept as a coarse re-measured floor. RUNTIME CONFIRMATION OWED TO THE OWNER: nobody has heard this. It is an audio change and needs an ear on the player.

title: SourceGuard's write-refusal has two holes
detail: Both holes reproduced. HOLE ONE: resolve_for_guard resolved .. lexically and symlinks not at all, so containment was decided by how a path is SPELLED rather than where it LEADS -- ln -s ~/aeon /tmp/tree then --out /tmp/tree/games/.../ojz.bin resolved to a path starting /tmp, matched no protected root, and landed inside the tree the guard exists to protect. Repaired as two named halves because neither suffices alone: resolve_lexically (needed because canonicalize refuses a file that is not there yet, which is every file this tool creates, and because aeon/../scratch/x must not read as inside aeon) then follow_existing_symlinks, which canonicalizes the longest EXISTING prefix and re-attaches the not-yet-existing tail verbatim -- the tail is the part being created so it has no links to follow; the prefix is where a link hides. Falls back to the lexical path when nothing resolves: weaker, never wrong. HOLE TWO: guard_for_inputs got the ROM and listing only while the module's own opening paragraph names THE FIXTURE'S neighbours (sonic3k.state0, sonic3k.srm) as the thing protected. --fixture-bin is the file the repair rewrites and can sit in a different checkout from the ROM; that checkout was unprotected. New guard_for_run(rom, lst, fixture, ...) assembles the list in the module rather than at the call site, which is what lets a test see which inputs a run protects. The module doc and the refusal message both said 'the ROM and listing'; both now say what is true, and the message says the path resolves there AFTER SYMLINKS -- a user reading a /tmp path in a refusal about ~/aeon otherwise cannot understand it. Two tests: the symlink one carries the clause that the LEXICAL resolution must NOT start with the repo, so it cannot pass without following the link; the fixture one uses two SEPARATE fake repositories plus a None-fixture control in which that repo is NOT protected, so the assertion is about the new argument and not about the discovery walk reaching everything anyway. Red-first, both mutations quoted from disk and reverted. title: The most-repeated safety claim in the tree names a mechanism that does not exist
detail: Reproduced, and the packet's count was a FLOOR: the claim is repeated in ELEVEN source comments, not eight -- render.rs (the LayerMask type doc, render_scanline's own doc, and the guard test's doc), oracle-player machine.rs x2 and bus.rs x2, oracle-aether engine.rs x3, oracle-frontend main.rs. VACUITY PROVEN EMPIRICALLY, not argued: the exact forbidden shape was planted on disk -- pub fn render_scanline_masked(&mut self, line: u16, mask: LayerMask) calling resolve_line_masked and committing overflow && mask.sprites, i.e. a mask reaching the sprite latch -- and the whole tree stayed green: cargo test -p oracle-core --lib 891 passed 0 failed, cargo clippy -p oracle-core --all-targets -D warnings clean, cargo fmt --check clean. Nothing in the workspace notices. Mutation quoted from disk via git diff --stat before the run and restored with git checkout HEAD -- from the committed baseline. STRUCTURAL OPTION INVESTIGATED AND RULED OUT, per d-47's 'investigate first'. The general reason: Rust's type system constrains programs under a given signature; it cannot constrain edits to the signature, and 'this function may never gain a parameter' is a claim about future edits. Concretely, no seal or privacy boundary can carry it -- LayerMask is pub by necessity (oracle-aether, oracle-frontend and oracle-player all construct masks) and is declared in the same module as render_scanline. Two candidate mechanisms were priced and both fail: (a) an opaque SpriteLatches token constructible only by the mask-blind sprite_line and required by commit_scanline_sprites, which dies on commit_scanline_sprites being public API that oracle-aether/tests/vdp_registers.rs:221 deliberately calls with hand-made bools -- a constructor for that test re-opens the hole; (b) moving LayerMask to a crate oracle-core does not depend on, which would work but the mask is consumed inside Vdp::rr9_winner, so it is a rewrite of the priority contest, not small. Anything that would truly gate the signature is a lint or compile-fail harness, excluded by d-47 and the ceremony moratorium. WHAT THE INVESTIGATION FOUND INSTEAD: a real mechanism already there. Every mask-taking render on Vdp takes &self (resolve_line_masked, render_line_masked, render_line_report_masked, pixel_attribution_masked); render_scanline is the ONLY &mut self render in render.rs; commit_scanline_sprites takes &mut self; and oracle-core is #![forbid(unsafe_code)] with no interior mutability (zero Cell/RefCell/Mutex/Atomic/UnsafeCell in the crate). So a masked render cannot compile a call to the latch commit -- the borrow checker, in exactly the shape of the correct example the finding pointed at (Engine::read_vdp_registers' peek property: &Vdp handed out where control_read_status needs &mut). LayerMask is also a parameter and never a field: the type does not occur in vdp.rs or system.rs at all, so no Vdp/System holds one and it is in no snapshot or state_hash input. The invariant is written as 'no render that takes a LayerMask takes &mut self', NOT as 'there is exactly one stateful render' -- deliberate, and the clause the hub's C5/H26 sequencing rule (main 6b0b75e) needs: a cheap second UNMASKED stateful render makes the second sentence false and leaves the property intact, so 'may a twin exist at all' is yes for an unmasked one and no for a masked one. All eleven sites now state the split -- what the compiler enforces vs what review holds -- and point the harm at a NAMED EXISTING test, masked_renders_leave_the_committed_sprite_latches_untouched, rather than at a paragraph. Both absolutist escalations ('must never gain one', 'none may ever be added') are gone. No new test machinery, no new dev-dependency. Verified: cargo test -p oracle-core --lib 891 passed 0 failed; -p oracle-aether --lib 92 passed; -p oracle-player --bins 402 passed; -p oracle-frontend --lib 125 passed and --bins 268 passed 1 ignored; clippy over all four crates --all-targets -D warnings clean; cargo fmt --check clean. RUSTDOC CONTROL: cargo doc -D warnings has 7 pre-existing errors in render.rs (private-item links); the HEAD~1 baseline was re-run and shows the SAME 7, line-shifted by this diff, so the four new intra-doc links add none. OPS: a fresh worktree has no vendor/, and 8 oracle-frontend save_state tests fail on the missing test ROM until vendor/ is symlinked in -- the failure message says so itself. docs/OVERSEER.md:694 states the claim too and is NOT touched here (boot doc, byte-bounded); replacement wording handed to the hub. Historical dated docs and OVERSEER-LOG.md repeat it as record and are left as record. oracle-frontend pick.rs's mirror-image claim ('resolve takes a LayerMask and there is no unmasked twin') is NOT part of this family: it states an API fact and already names a real parity guard.

title: Every replay frame renders a full attributed scanline and discards it, to produce three status bits
detail: Reproduced exactly as filed, and the mechanism the finding implies is the mechanism that is there. deliver_event's Scanline arm called Vdp::render_scanline unconditionally and only THEN asked the sink whether anyone wanted the rows; oracle-replay composes Fanout<StopWhen, StopWhen> (runner.rs:547) and overrides neither wants_scanlines, so every one of its 1176 frames composited 224 fully attributed scanlines and dropped all 224 -- 263,424 discarded rasters per playthrough. FIX: Vdp::advance_scanline, the picture-free twin -- same sprite walk, same three committed bits (R10 dot-overflow carry, sprite-overflow latch, collision latch), no composite, no LineReport, no pixels; the Scanline arm branches on wants_scanlines() and takes it when unarmed. THE EQUIVALENCE IS STRUCTURAL, not empirical, which is what made this fix small: in resolve_line_masked the sprite pipeline runs FIRST and UNCONDITIONALLY -- above the display-enable early return and above the composite -- and all three bits are products of that one call; everything the composite adds feeds ResolvedLine::pixels and nothing else; line_report_from reads only registers plus the already-built SpriteLine; and all of it is &self in a crate that is forbid(unsafe_code) with no interior mutability, so none of it can perturb a field the sprite walk reads. The one carried field, sprite_dot_overflow_carry, is read in exactly ONE place in the module (sprite_line's seen_nonzero seed) and written in exactly ONE (commit_scanline_sprites); the twin preserves their order -- read at entry, written at exit, nothing between. THE NUMBER d-44 ASKED FOR: replay_runner over s4.debug.bin + s4.debug.lst, 1176 frames, before/after binaries interleaved run-by-run in one session so machine drift hits both arms. Two independent sessions, 11 and 9 reps: before med 2548.5 / 2556.3 ms, after med 989.2 / 986.9 ms -- 2.58x and 2.59x by median, 2.61x by min in both. The discarded raster was ~61% of the replay's entire wall clock. Output is BYTE-IDENTICAL between arms across all 40 runs, register dump included, which over 1176 frames of a real ROM is a differential equivalence check on top of the unit guard. GUARD: render.rs the_cheap_scanline_advance_leaves_the_same_machine -- eight consecutive lines through both paths over fourteen fixtures (H40/H32 x one-sprite / collision-only / count overflow / dot overflow / R10 x=0 masking / display-disabled / the 256..320 band), asserting whole-Vdp PartialEq after EACH line: every field, not the three bits. THREE RED CELLS, mutations quoted from disk and restored from a committed baseline: (A) drop commit_scanline_sprites -> red naming 'H32 collision only'; (B) commit collision as false -> red, same case; (C) width hardcoded to 256 -> red naming 'H40 collision in the 256..320 band'. (C) WAS GREEN ON THE FIRST CORPUS, and that is the transferable part: width reaches nothing but draw_sprite's buffer clip, so it is observable in committed state through collision alone and only for pixels in x in [256,320) -- the band H40 has and H32 does not. Every original fixture stacked sprites at x 0 or laid non-overlapping ones across x 0..384, so none put an OVERLAP in that band, and the coverage assertion 'saw_h32 && saw_h40' was TRUE the whole time while answering a different question than it looked like it answered. A corpus can exercise both values of a parameter and still be unable to distinguish them. Fixed by deriving the discriminator (WIDE_BAND_X = 280) and asserting a control BEFORE the sweep that the pair collides at 320 and is clipped at 256 -- separate on purpose, because the sweep compares two paths and stays green whenever BOTH are wrong the same way, which is exactly what happened (commit 8b79136). POSITIVE CONTROL ON THE ARMED ARM: swapping the armed arm to commit-then-resolve (the reseed error report_rgb's doc warns about) turns scanline_golden_scorecard RED, so the currency is sensitive to this region and the armed arm's zero-diff is a measured statement, not an assumption. H26 PAIRING DISCHARGED: its resolution was worded 'the invariant is no render taking a LayerMask takes &mut self, deliberately NOT there is exactly one stateful render' precisely to admit this parcel's twin. The twin now exists, so the prose that reasoned about there being one moved with it -- render_scanline's canonical doc names advance_scanline as the case it was written to admit, and the four sites that said 'the one render that commits the latches' (oracle-player machine.rs, oracle-frontend main.rs, oracle-aether engine.rs x2) carry the correction marker. advance_scanline takes no LayerMask; a masked twin of either stateful render stays forbidden. SCOPE, AND THE FINDING WAS NOT A FLOOR HERE: oracle-player (machine.rs:158,165), oracle-frontend (bus.rs:638,644) and oracle-aether (engine.rs:2685,3037; host.rs:1452,1458) put ScanlineCapture in the Fanout on BOTH branches of every run path, so all three are armed by construction and pay the raster for a picture they actually display. oracle-replay is the only production consumer that was unarmed. The tree's own null-sink run_frames call sites (~30, all in test modules) take the cheap path now too. CURRENCY: zero movement. crates/oracle-core/tests/ has ONE file touched, scanline_capture.rs, and only its module doc-comment, which claimed the default path is 'byte-identical to before: same render_scanline call' and would otherwise have shipped false. No golden, no pin, no fixture byte moved. VERIFIED: cargo fmt --check clean; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean TWICE; cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast = 88 legs / 2757 passed / 0 failed / 6 ignored. The brief's baseline of '88 legs, 2759 passed, 3 ignored' cannot come from the debug command it was printed with: oracle-replay's three full playthroughs are cfg_attr(debug_assertions, ignore), so a debug run reports 6 ignored and a release run reports 3. Reconciled exactly -- 2757 + those 3 = 2760 = 2759 baseline + this parcel's one new test -- and the three were run under ./tools/replay_playthroughs.sh (release): 16 passed, 0 failed, including all three playthroughs through the new cheap path.
